videos.title: One-click background removal just got way smarter with this AI.
videos.ai_tech_id: GPT Image 2.5 (OpenAI) background removal / transparency handling
summary: Futurepedia highlights an upgrade to GPT Image 2.5's one-click background removal, showing that it now handles genuinely complex transparency, subjects like jellyfish bells and dragonfly wings that need to look convincingly see-through rather than just cut out.

The clip demonstrates that the updated remove-background button preserves subtle lighting effects such as the glow around a subject, a detail the previous version of the model reportedly lost when isolating an object from its background.

For the hardest cases, heavy transparency across an entire body rather than just edges, Futurepedia recommends prompting for the effect directly instead of relying on the one-click button, framing this as a practical workflow tip for anyone using GPT Image 2.5 for product or nature photography edits.

videos.title: Should You Switch From Claude To ChatGPT?
videos.ai_tech_id: Claude / Claude Code (Anthropic) vs. ChatGPT Work & Codex (OpenAI) automation and image workflows
summary: Sabrina Ramonov addresses whether people should switch from Claude to ChatGPT, opening with the position that most users should not migrate and that her own switch was driven by two specific, narrow pain points rather than a general endorsement of one platform over the other.

Her first reason was consolidation: Claude's scheduled tasks and Claude Code's routines were split across surfaces and the routines lacked browser access, whereas ChatGPT Work and Codex keep her automations together with an in-app browser that handles logged-in workflows without needing API access. Her second reason was native image generation, ChatGPT's canvas lets her generate, edit, and iterate on images in one place, a workflow she found added friction inside Claude.

She also describes the mechanics of the migration itself, noting that Claude skills stored in a `.skills` folder map fairly cleanly onto Codex `.agents`, and that she used ChatGPT to convert them while simultaneously simplifying older automation workarounds, closing with the caveat that switching only makes sense if a viewer's own workflow hits the same two specific pain points.

videos.title: How To Get Your First AI Consulting Clients
videos.ai_tech_id: General AI consulting/coaching business advice (references ChatGPT and Claude as the tools being taught)
summary: Sabrina Ramonov lays out where first-time AI consultants should look for their earliest clients: their warm network, defined broadly to include past coworkers, old classmates, club members, neighbors, local business owners, other creators, and friends of friends, not just immediate contacts.

Her recommended first move is public visibility, posting what you're personally learning, the tools you're testing, the automations you're building, the prompts you're using, and small workflow wins, followed by a simple, low-pressure ask inviting referrals from people who know someone needing help with tools like ChatGPT and Claude.

The underlying logic is that warm contacts already trust the poster and need less proof than a cold lead would, so some will ask for help directly while others will refer someone else; she frames these early warm-network wins as the proof needed to later attract colder, less familiar audiences.
